# hypothesis: An __exit__ annotated to return Literal[True] swallows ValueError, so run(True) returns the value assigned before the raise at runtime, while checkers may treat x as always reassigned after the with block.
from types import TracebackType
from typing import Literal, reveal_type


class Swallow:
    def __enter__(self) -> None:
        return None

    def __exit__(
        self,
        exc_type: type[BaseException] | None,
        exc: BaseException | None,
        tb: TracebackType | None,
    ) -> Literal[True]:
        return True


def run(fail: bool) -> int | None:
    x: int | None = None
    with Swallow():
        x = 1
        if fail:
            raise ValueError('boom')
        x = 2
    reveal_type(x)
    return x


assert run(True) == 1
assert run(False) == 2
hypothesis: An __exit__ typed to return Literal[True] swallows the ValueError, so run(True) returns 1 at runtime, while a checker may narrow x after the block as if the block always completed.
